text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London finished higher after a spate of fund buying boosted the market. August closed at $330.50 per tonne, a gain of $2.70, while October closed $2.80 higher at $321.30 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York climbed to new contract highs for the second straight session as an increasingly solid technical outlook drew speculative buyers into the market. July added 14 points to close at 11.48 cents/lb. October closed at 11.29 cents/lb, a gain of 10 points. The outer months closed 6 points higher. The market looks increasingly overbought as the rise is purely technical without fundamental support.

INDONESIA - Indonesia is expected to produce 2.1 million tonnes of plantation white sugar in 1997, up from 2.095 million tonnes produced the previous year. Production in 1998 is expected to remain stagnant. Molasses production in 1997 is put at 1.155 million tonnes, down from 1.157 million tonnes the previous year.

CANADA - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 43,346 tonnes, raw value, down from 106,758 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 537,794 tonnes compared to 632,192 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 were 1.160 million tonnes against 1.013 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/March 1996/97 were Australia with 441,816 tonnes raws against 397,659 tonnes, Brazil with 53,578 tonnes compared to 24,500 tonnes and Cuba with 30,900 tonnes against 81,743 tonnes.

ITALY - Sugar imports in January 1997 reached 20,134 tonnes, raw value, down from 26,270 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first six months of 1996/97 (August/January) up to 190,550 tonnes compared to 142,313 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 379,026 tonnes against 266,279 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in August/January 1996/97 were Germany with 78,586 tonnes whites against 34,546 tonnes, France with 45,202 tonnes, down from 60,412 tonnes and Brazil with 14,149 tonnes compared to 5,622 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January 1997 reached 9,962 tonnes, up from 2,364 tonnes in January 1996. Cumulative exports since the start of the 1996/97 campaign (August) amounted to 75,551 tonnes, down from 141,370 tonnes in 1995/96.
